gap: No result ChatGPT got states what RAM costs in November 2026. TerraMaster's own store lists 16 GB DDR5 at $469.99, and on Amazon 16 GB DDR5 SO-DIMMs run $257–280 while 8 GB DDR4 runs $57–70. So taking a DDR5 box to 16 GB (the DXP2800, which has one slot) costs about two-thirds of the $389.99 box price, while bringing the DDR4 F2-423 from 4 GB to 12 GB costs about $60.
standout_why: Compared against Starry Hope's Best Budget NAS (updated 2026-11-02), Bitdoze's Best NAS for Homelab (2026-09-21) and the TerraMaster F2-424 page ChatGPT cited. Starry Hope gives box prices and RAM ceilings (DXP2800 16 GB max, F2-425 16 GB max). Bitdoze gives the DXP2800 at $339.99 (Oct 23). Neither prices a RAM upgrade. ChatGPT itself said 'I'd budget for a RAM upgrade' on the F2-423 and gave no amount. The TechRadar F2-424 review came back truncated and could not be read.
decides: This confirms the budget split. If the $400 has to cover the whole lab, the F2-423 (4 GB DDR4, sold on Newegg but no longer on TerraMaster's US store) plus an 8 GB DDR4 stick at about $57–70 gets to 12 GB for less than the DXP2800 alone. For DDR5 machines (DXP2800, F2-424, F2-425 Plus), the RAM they ship with is the RAM a beginner should plan to keep: 8 GB on the DXP2800 at $389.99 and 8 GB on the F2-425 Plus at $399.49. Going to 16 GB adds $257 or more and breaks the cap. The F2-424 is out of stock on TerraMaster's store, so it should not be a pick.
candidates: Used Dell OptiPlex / Lenovo ThinkCentre Micro
